reads.need: The city hires far more people than it houses
reads.evidence: 2,728 open postings in 30 days against 7,437 households: about 37 postings for every 100 households. The city puts its daytime population near 70,000 against 16,379 residents.
reads.quality: Most of the people who work here drive in. That is traffic, parking and lunch-hour crowding for residents, and long commutes for the workers.
reads.move: Count who commutes in and from where, then test what would let more of them live or stay nearby: shuttles from the Metro stations, housing near the job centers, evening reasons to stay.
reads.why: The postings count is ours and the daytime figure is the city's round number. The direction is safe; the exact ratio is not.

reads.evidence: 902 of the 2,728 postings have Engineer in the title, a third of all openings. Technicians and trades are 60.
reads.quality: The best-paid work in town asks for a degree and often a security clearance. Residents without those have a much shorter list.
reads.move: Map the routes into aerospace that do not start with an engineering degree: harness, composites and test technician roles at the same employers, and where the training for them is taught.
reads.why: Title matching is blunt. An Engineer posting can be software, sales or facilities.

reads.need: Almost nothing posted for care, teaching or food
reads.evidence: 8 nursing and care postings, 11 food and hospitality, none for teaching.
reads.quality: These are the jobs that make a town work for families and older residents. Few postings can mean the jobs are filled, or that they are hired by word of mouth and never reach the feed we read.
reads.move: Ask directly. A short survey of schools, clinics, care homes and restaurants would settle whether this is a real shortage or a blind spot in the data.
reads.why: Our source is LinkedIn-based and undercounts small employers, restaurants and schools.

gaps: What the posted jobs pay. The feed carries no wages, so we cannot yet say which openings cover local rent.
Where workers commute from. The Census publishes this (LEHD) and it has not been pulled in.
